title: finding(types): objectui#7759 group B — `SliderSchema.defaultValue` declaration narrower than its read site, `TooltipSchema.content` mirror wider than its read site
body:
Execution split of objectstack-ai/objectui#7759, **group B (SINGLE-OR-LIST)**. It is split out because the ruling says to execute per group: 「按组开 PR,每组一 changeset」 (director ruling issuecomment-5617465269, plus the ordering note 5617614225). This is not a new finding and needs no new ruling. Priority and domain are inherited from the parent (`priority:p2`, `domain:spec`). Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01877XiBYSaRCk2CU7cMSg3S`, so that group E (dispatched on the parent itself) and this group each have their own claim and PR.

## The keys (re-measured on `origin/main` `32bf2d6f`, ledger `WIDER_ARMS` in `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`)

| pair | key | spec declares it? | direction under ruling rule 2 (objectui-own ⇒ read site is truth) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form.zod.ts#SliderSchema` | `defaultValue` | no | **widen the TS declaration** to the single-or-list the mirror already accepts. The renderer deliberately normalizes a scalar (ruling B1; renderer reads at 5596479859). |
| `overlay.zod.ts#TooltipSchema` | `content` | no | **narrow the mirror** to the declared union. The array arm would throw 「Objects are not valid as a React child」 at the read site. |
| `form.zod.ts#SliderSchema` | `value` | no | no read site: goes on the ADR-0049 retirement worklist (ruling: 「`Slider.value` 无人读 ⇒ 退役清单」). ⛔ Not in this card's changeset unless the dev re-measures it and it is a one-line tombstone under the 2026-08-27 immediate-retirement rule; say which in the report. |

The spec-declared check was a search of `@objectstack/spec` source for `SliderSchema` / `TooltipSchema`: 0 hits for either.

## Done when

The rows for these keys leave `WiderThanDeclared` / `WIDER_ARMS`, each change carries a pin that reddens on revert, and there is one `@object-ui/types` changeset (`minor`, Clause-② yes: the accept set narrows on one face and widens on the other).
